articles.body: 미국 7월 비농업 고용이 예상과 달리 23,000명 감소했으나, 연준 금리 인상 부담 완화로 해석되며 S&P 500이 사상 최고치를 경신했다.

articles.headline: 버크셔 해서웨이, 3년 만에 순매수 전환…애벌 CEO, 버핏 현금 200억불 투입
articles.eng: Berkshire Hathaway Turns Net Buyer After 3 Years…CEO Abel Deploys $20 Billion of Buffett's Cash
articles.body: 그렉 애벌 버크셔 해서웨이 CEO가 3년 이상 이어진 매도 기조를 끝내고 200억 달러 규모 순매수로 전환. 버핏의 현금 더미를 마침내 운용 시작.

articles.headline: 마이크로소프트, 美 기업 사상 최대 일일 시총 증가…$4,500억 ↑
articles.eng: Microsoft Posts Largest Single-Day Market Cap Gain for Any US Company…$450 Billion Increase
articles.body: MS가 하루 만에 시가총액 4,500억 달러 증가하며 미국 기업 사상 최대 일일 시총 증가 기록. Azure 클라우드 매출 1,000억 달러 돌파.

articles.headline: 환율 1,407.89원…1,300원대 진입 눈앞, 원화 강세 지속
articles.eng: KRW at 1,407.89 per Dollar…1,300 Range in Sight, Won Strengthening Continues
articles.body: 원/달러 환율이 1,600원대에서 급락해 1,407.89원까지 하락. 1,300원대 진입을 앞두고 있으며 수출주 채산성에 영향 예상.

articles.headline: 중국 7월 물가 상승세 둔화…이란發 유가 충격 완화
articles.eng: China's July Inflation Cools…Impact from Iran Oil Shock Eases
articles.body: 중국의 7월 소비자물가 상승률이 둔화. 이란 호르무즈 사태로 인한 유가 충격이 완화되고 있다는 분석.

articles.headline: 아시아 하이브리드 차량, 美 시장서 판매 20% 급증…고유가 수혜
articles.eng: Asian Hybrid Vehicles See 20% Surge in US Sales…Benefiting from High Gas Prices
articles.body: 혼다·현대·도요타 등 아시아 자동차 제조사의 하이브리드 차량이 미국에서 전년 대비 20% 판매 증가. 고유가로 인한 연비 중시 소비 트렌드.

articles.headline: 메타, 아동 SNS 유해 콘텐츠로 10억 달러 벌금…사상 최대 규모
articles.eng: Meta Fined Nearly $1 Billion Over Social Media Harm to Children…Largest Ever
articles.body: 메타가 아동·청소년 대상 SNS 유해 콘텐츠 문제로 약 10억 달러 벌금 부과. 역대 최대 규모의 SNS 규제 벌금.

articles.headline: Microsoft Posts Biggest One-Day Market-Cap Gain for Any U.S. Company
articles.body: Microsoft gained $450 billion in market value in a single day — the largest one-day gain for any U.S. company — while Meta shares plunged. Azure cloud revenue surpassed $100 billion annually.

articles.headline: Kevin Warsh's Honeymoon With the Bond Market Is Already Over
articles.body: Investors warned that the Fed under Chair Kevin Warsh must show commitment to the inflation fight after Wednesday's bond market selloff. The 'bear steepener' is not a Goldilocks moment for stocks.

articles.headline: Big Oil Is Reaping Rewards From the Chaos in Energy Markets
articles.body: ExxonMobil's earnings doubled and Chevron posted its highest quarterly earnings on record as energy prices soared during the prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: The U.S. Commander With a Two-Week Plan to Escalate Strikes in Iran
articles.body: A U.S. military commander has developed a two-week plan to escalate strikes in Iran, as tensions remain high over the Strait of Hormuz closure and nuclear negotiations.

articles.headline: Trump's Immigration Push Keeps Expanding With New $100,000 Fee Idea
articles.body: The Trump administration is considering a new $100,000 fee as part of its expanding immigration enforcement. The proposal would add to birthright citizenship restrictions already being pursued.

articles.headline: Anthropic AI Models Hacked Three Companies During Tests
articles.body: Anthropic's AI models successfully hacked into three companies during controlled security tests, raising concerns about AI safety. Banks are in talks to lend $15 billion for an Anthropic data center backed by Google.

articles.headline: The Rise of Million-Dollar Companies With Just One Employee
articles.body: AI tools are enabling solo entrepreneurs to build million-dollar businesses with no employees, signaling a fundamental shift in how companies are structured and scaled.

articles.headline: Trump Administration to End Medicare Drug Plan Subsidy
articles.body: The Trump administration is moving to end a Medicare drug plan subsidy, a significant change to prescription drug coverage for seniors.

articles.headline: Oil Futures on Track for Big Monthly Gains
articles.body: Oil futures turned higher and were on track for hefty gains for July, which saw the U.S.-Iran Memorandum of Understanding fall apart and Iran resume attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: Iran Talks Offer Little Relief for Hormuz Shipping
articles.body: Iran's negotiations with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz offer little immediate relief for shipping. Iran demands US troop withdrawal and war reparations before fully reopening the strategic waterway.

articles.headline: Berkshire Hathaway Spends Down Cash Pile Under CEO Greg Abel
articles.body: Greg Abel finally puts Warren Buffett's massive cash pile to work, ending a three-year selling streak with a net $20 billion deployment into stocks and $4.5 billion in buybacks.

articles.headline: Trump Again Moves to Fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook, Reviving Independence Fight
articles.body: President Trump has renewed his attempt to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, reigniting concerns about the central bank's political independence.

articles.headline: Behind Bessent Moves, Wall Street Sees Sign of Bond-Market Angst
articles.body: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's recent moves are being interpreted by Wall Street as signs of growing anxiety in the bond market. The US government's euro sale to prop up the yen blindsided the ECB.

articles.headline: US Economy Unexpectedly Sheds 23,000 Jobs in July
articles.body: The US economy unexpectedly lost 23,000 jobs in July, far below the expected gain of 88,000. Markets interpreted the weak data positively as reducing pressure for further Fed rate hikes.

articles.headline: Barrick Chairman's Planned Overhaul Meets Investor Backlash
articles.body: A Goldman Sachs veteran's plan to split Barrick Gold is encountering strong investor opposition. Gold prices are near $4,400/oz, making the mining giant's strategic direction critical.

articles.headline: Turkey Resumes Black Sea Ship Transits Via Straits After Delays
articles.body: Turkey has resumed ship transits through the Black Sea straits after delays. This comes as Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan sign a new 'Mecca Joint Defense Agreement.'

articles.headline: Paramount Will Put 30-Film Pledge in Writing to Theater Chains
articles.body: Paramount Pictures is committing in writing to produce at least 30 films annually for theatrical release, reassuring theater chains amid Warner Bros.' interest in acquiring the studio.

articles.headline: Apple Explores Shaking Up Its Smartwatch for a New Era
articles.body: Apple is exploring a major redesign of its Apple Watch as the company prepares for its September iPhone event. The overhaul signals a new era for the wearable device.

articles.headline: The U.S. Is Burning Through Weapons in Iran. Russia and China Are Taking Note.
articles.body: A more drawn-out Iran conflict benefits Moscow and Beijing, as the U.S. rapidly depletes its weapons stockpiles. Patriot missile inventory is reportedly below 1,700 units.

articles.headline: A Mysterious Crypto Entrepreneur Bought $100 Million in Trump Tokens
articles.body: Guren 'Bobby' Zhou, a failed retail store owner turned crypto entrepreneur, bought $100 million in digital tokens from President Trump's crypto business. Questions raised about World Liberty Financial's vetting process.

articles.headline: Taiwan Bets on Drones to Deter China, Inspired by Ukraine
articles.body: Inspired by Ukraine's battlefield gains, Taiwan is betting on drones as a key deterrent against a potential invasion by China. The island is rapidly expanding its unmanned aerial capabilities.

articles.headline: Has America Already Undergone a Soft Breakup?
articles.body: Kurt Andersen argues that America may have already experienced a 'soft breakup' along political lines, with Democrats and Republicans living in increasingly separate realities.

articles.headline: A Generation on Antidepressants Searches for the Exit
articles.body: A generation raised on SSRIs is now questioning long-term antidepressant use, exploring the side effects and searching for ways to safely discontinue medication.

articles.headline: Mike Rogers Suggests Further Scrutiny of 2020 Election
articles.body: Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers suggested further scrutiny of the 2020 election and claimed voting irregularities sank his first Senate bid, raising concerns about election denialism in key races.

articles.headline: Forget the East Wing. The Real Demolition Has Only Just Begun.
articles.body: Paul Goldberger writes that the Trump administration's changes to Washington landmarks go beyond the East Wing — the real architectural and institutional 'demolition' is just beginning.

articles.headline: Growing Up in Peru, I Thought I Knew Poverty. America Surprised Me.
articles.body: Nicholas Kristof contrasts poverty in Peru with surprising forms of deprivation he has witnessed in America, challenging assumptions about wealth and social safety nets.

articles.headline: Groceries Are Expensive in America. Here's How 5 Shoppers Are Adjusting.
articles.body: An interactive feature documenting how five American shoppers are coping with persistently high grocery prices, with strategies ranging from bulk buying to changing dietary habits.

articles.headline: Senate Narrowly Approves Todd Blanche as AG, Capping Tough Confirmation Fight
articles.body: The Senate narrowly confirmed Todd Blanche as Attorney General after a tough confirmation battle. Sen. Lisa Murkowski opposed the nomination, citing concerns over Blanche's ties to Trump.

articles.headline: Iran Says Hormuz Deal with Oman Won't Fully Reopen Strait
articles.body: Iran says its deal with Oman is close but will not fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices jumped after senior Iranian officials demanded US troop withdrawal and war reparations as conditions.

articles.headline: Trump Administration Has Refunded $100 Billion in Tariffs. Will You Get Any?
articles.body: Major corporations are getting hundreds of millions of dollars in tariff refunds from the Trump administration, but most individual consumers are unlikely to see any money back.

articles.headline: Russia Keeps Testing NATO. The Lack of Response Will Embolden Putin.
articles.body: Russia continues probing NATO defenses with apparent impunity. The lack of strong response could embolden Putin as Ukraine runs out of missile interceptors, with 17 Ukrainians killed in overnight Russian strikes.

articles.headline: White House Drafting Order Linking Vaccines to Autism Despite Pollsters' Warnings
articles.body: The White House is drafting an executive order linking vaccines to autism, despite warnings from its own pollsters about potential public backlash and scientific consensus against such claims.

articles.headline: On Hiroshima Anniversary, Japan's Premier Shifts Tone on Nuclear Policy
articles.body: Ultraconservative Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi left a subtle opening in Hiroshima anniversary remarks for rethinking Japan's 'Three Non-Nuclear Principles,' potentially signaling a historic policy shift.

articles.headline: Scrutiny of Dominion Energy Megamerger Intensifies as Virginia Governor Weighs In
articles.body: Governor Abigail Spanberger said she is 'deeply skeptical' of the $67 billion proposal to sell Virginia's biggest power company to a Florida firm, intensifying scrutiny of the megamerger.

articles.headline: TPS for Haitians Officially Ends, Putting Thousands Out of Work and in Limbo
articles.body: A federal judge allowed the Trump administration to terminate temporary protected status for 350,000 Haitians. ICE has begun outfitting Haitian immigrants with ankle monitors.

articles.headline: The Senate Wants a Recess. Trump Doesn't.
articles.body: Before senators leave for recess, Republican leaders are trying to push through a lengthy to-do list. The conflict highlights ongoing tensions between the legislative and executive branches.

articles.headline: Tehran Says US Must Meet New Conditions Before Iran Reopens Strait
articles.body: Iranian rhetoric hardens amid push to seal deal between Islamic republic and Oman that would reopen the Hormuz waterway. Iran demands the US 'rectify its behaviour' first. Iranian missile targets UAE tanker despite talks.

articles.headline: Greg Abel Finally Puts Buffett's Cash Pile to Work
articles.body: Berkshire Hathaway chief Greg Abel ends more than three-year selling streak, ploughing a net $20 billion into stocks. This marks a historic shift from the Buffett era's cautious approach.

articles.headline: America's New Oligarchy
articles.body: An in-depth analysis of how America's wealth concentration has created a new oligarchic class with unprecedented influence over politics, media, and technology sectors.

articles.headline: Trump Is Dismantling US Guardrails, Warn Former Security Officials
articles.body: Former national security officials warn that President Trump is systematically dismantling institutional guardrails that have protected American democracy and its global alliances for decades.

articles.headline: US Economy Unexpectedly Sheds 23,000 Jobs in July
articles.body: The US economy unexpectedly lost 23,000 jobs in July, far below expectations of a gain of 88,000. Markets rallied on the data as it eased pressure for further Fed rate hikes.

articles.headline: Investors Return to European Stocks as Strong Earnings Lift Iran War Gloom
articles.body: Companies in the Stoxx Europe 600 are on track to deliver a 22% increase in Q2 profits, drawing investors back to European equities despite ongoing Iran war concerns.

articles.headline: Asian Carmakers Cash In as High Petrol Prices Lift US Demand for Hybrids
articles.body: Sales of hybrid vehicles made by Honda, Hyundai, and Toyota jump by a fifth in July as high US petrol prices — driven by the Iran crisis — shift consumer preferences toward fuel-efficient vehicles.

articles.headline: Google's AI Shake-up Boosts Brin as DeepMind's Hassabis Steps Aside
articles.body: Google co-founder Sergey Brin takes a more active role in AI development as DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis steps aside in a major shake-up of the tech giant's artificial intelligence strategy.

articles.headline: Landmark Crypto Bill Stalls in US Senate Despite $225 Million Spending Push
articles.body: The cryptocurrency industry's top legislative priority has stalled in the Senate despite $225 million in lobbying spending, as lawmakers spar over provisions in the landmark bill.
